problems.title: Cancel cubic terms before factoring
problems.question: Solve (x+2)(x²-2x+4)+3x²=x²(x+2)-2x+8.
steps: Cancel x³+8 from both sides, leaving 3x²=2x²-2x.
Thus x²+2x=x(x+2)=0.

problems.title: Read every feature of a piecewise-linear graph
problems.question: From the printed graph find domain, range, decreasing intervals, and the number of zeros.
problems.idea: Read endpoints and vertices against the unit grid.
formulas: Domain consists of plotted x-values; range of plotted y-values; zeros are crossings of y=0.
steps: The vertices are (-4,2),(0,-2),(2,3),(4,-3),(6,1). The endpoints are included, so the domain is [-4,6].
The lowest ordinate is -3 and highest 3, giving range [-3,3].
The graph decreases from -4 to 0 and from 2 to 4.
Each of the four segments crosses the x-axis once, giving four zeros.
problems.answer: Domain [-4,6]; range [-3,3]; decreasing on [-4,0] and [2,4]; four zeros.

problems.title: Polynomial division with a remainder
problems.question: Divide x⁶-3x⁵-x⁴+2x³+3x²+x-3 by x-3.
steps: The coefficient list is 1,-3,-1,2,3,1,-3.
Successive synthetic-division results are 1,0,-1,-1,0,1, with final remainder 0.
Thus Q=x⁵-x³-x²+1.

problems.title: Recover two lines from axis intercepts
problems.question: Find the intersection F of the two lines drawn in the coordinate plane.
formulas: Slope=(change in y)/(change in x); solve the two line equations.
steps: The rising line passes through (-1,0),(0,1), so y=x+1.
The falling line passes through (0,3),(2,0), so y=3-3x/2.
Set x+1=3-3x/2 to get x=4/5 and y=9/5.

problems.title: Use the correct intercepted arcs
problems.question: Chords AB,CD meet at M with AMD=50°. Arc BD exceeds arc AC by 10°. Find arc BD.
problems.idea: The 50° angle uses the other pair of arcs, AD and BC.
formulas: Intersecting-chord angle=half the sum of intercepted arcs; all four arcs sum to 360°.
steps: Arc AD+arc BC=100°. Therefore arc AC+arc BD=360°-100°=260°.
Put arc AC=t and arc BD=t+10°. Then 2t+10°=260°, so t=125°.
Arc BD=135°.
problems.note: Using arcs AC and BD directly in the 50° formula would select the supplementary angle and produce the wrong answer.

problems.title: An inradius identity forces equal legs
problems.question: In a right triangle, circumradius plus inradius equals one leg. Find the angles.
steps: Their sum is (a+b)/2. If this equals a, then b=a; if it equals b, then a=b.
Thus the right triangle has equal legs and two equal acute angles.

problems.title: A cube identity under a linear condition
problems.question: Given a+2b=1, prove a³+8b³=1-6ab.
problems.idea: Expand the cube of the known sum.
steps: Set u=a,v=2b. Then (a+2b)³=a³+8b³+6ab(a+2b).
Since a+2b=1, this becomes 1=a³+8b³+6ab.
Rearrange to the required identity.

problems.title: Incentre angle from arc ratios
problems.question: The arcs AC:CB:AB are 3:4:2. O is the incentre. Find BOC.
problems.idea: Find A from its opposite arc, then use the bisector angle.
formulas: Inscribed angle=half its intercepted arc; BOC=90°+A/2.
steps: The nine arc units make 360°, so arc CB=160° and A=80°.

problems.title: A perpendicular median forces a 2:1 side ratio
problems.question: A triangle has three consecutive positive-integer sides. One internal bisector is perpendicular to one median. Find the sides.
problems.idea: If they start at different vertices, a coordinate projection gives a doubled pair of sides.
formulas: Let the A-bisector be the x-axis, B=(c cosθ,c sinθ),C=(b cosθ,-b sinθ).
steps: A median from the same vertex cannot be perpendicular to its internal bisector, because its midpoint has a positive projection along that bisector.
For the B-median to be perpendicular, B and the midpoint of AC must have the same x-coordinate: c cosθ=(b/2)cosθ, so b=2c. Other labels give the same doubled-pair requirement.
Among n,n+1,n+2, a 2:1 pair gives n=1 or 2. The sides 1,2,3 are degenerate; 2,3,4 form a valid triangle and satisfy the projection condition.

problems.title: Maximize two bounded reciprocals together
problems.question: Maximize 3/(4x²-12xy+9y²+9)+1/(|x-2y-1|+6). Find x,y.
problems.idea: Each denominator has an independent minimum; check they can occur together.
steps: The first term is at most 3/9=1/3 and the second at most 1/6, so the sum is at most 1/2.
Equality requires 2x-3y=0 and x-2y-1=0.
Solve to get y=-2,x=-3, which makes both lower bounds hold.
